title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls, injection and retries
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR improves the ergonomics and reliability of tool/function calling when multiple tools are requested (multi-tool) and when those calls are executed in parallel. The main goals are: 1) make it straightforward to inject tool results into the model stream mid-response without destabilizing streaming, 2) add a robust retry/backoff policy for transient tool failures that preserves deterministic injection semantics, 3) support configurable parallel execution limits and ordering guarantees for multi-tool calls, and 4) update the OpenAI compatibility layer so function-calling behavior aligns with our extensions for parallel tool results and retries. The change is driven by customer reports of streaming glitches when a tool result is injected after partial streaming, edge cases where retries led to duplicate injections, and internal experiments showing that controlled parallelism reduces tail latency on common workloads. This is a backwards-compatible change: default behavior remains the same but new fields in the SDK/APIs allow finer control (parallelism_limit, inject_when_ready, retry_policy). The PR includes runtime changes (coordinator, streaming adapter), API surface updates (compat shim and SDK flags), unit and integration tests, and docs/upgrade notes. See commits and files for details.

review_comments: Derek Liu: Nice overall shape. Can we keep the default parallelism_limit to 1 in the compat layer so existing customers aren't surprised by different ordering?

Marta Novik: Injecting mid-stream is tricky for streaming clients: we need a clear resume token and a stable marker so SDKs can re-attach. Please add a small section in the doc with pseudocode for SDKs.
Rafael Gomez: The retry_policy config looks good but add explicit guidance on idempotency — which tool results are safe to retry? Add tests for non-idempotent tool behavior.

release_notes: Added opt-in support for parallel tool execution and safe mid-stream injection of tool results. New API flags: parallelism_limit (default 1 in compat layer), inject_when_ready (opt-in), retry_policy (configurable). Backwards compatible by default; see docs/migration.md for SDK changes and examples.
